The server-side form of `grep -E "^dir/"`, for a directory-ATTRIBUTION question `files` (suffix match) cannot express, e.g. "does ANY error fall under apps/operator-vite/?" (EI-22050606808498557). Combines with `files` as an OR: a diagnostic matching either is kept. `errorCount` is the filtered count; `totalErrorCount` the project-wide one.

timeoutMs.description: Hard budget for the compile. Default 300000ms, but a FOREGROUND run is clamped to 45000ms — below the ~55s MCP transport cap — so an over-long compile returns an actionable timeout instead of an opaque transport error. A project that needs longer (packages/operator-core is ~104s) KEEPS these structured diagnostics via scopeToFiles, or "npm run lint:tsc -- --files=..." for the baseline-gated verdict; a detached capability:inspect { run_in_background: true } run returns a raw LOG, not these diagnostics.

incremental.description: Allow tsc to use a warm tsconfig.tsbuildinfo. Default false — EI-487: an incremental run UNDER-reports errors in files the cache has not reindexed, which read as green for days. Only set true when you want a fast re-check and already know the tree is warm.

scopeToFiles.description: Check ONLY `files` instead of the whole project, so a run fits the foreground cap under fleet load. Requires `files`; each path may be repository-relative, relative to the selected project directory, or absolute. `engine` says who answered. engine:"tsc-service" — the shared typecheck service (when it serves this checkout and project): your files are checked inside the FULL program, and otherErrors cover files that reference their exported types or import them directly; measured 1.4s for a hub file. engine:"tsc-cli" (serviceFallback says why) — a throwaway program of `files` + their import graph, so otherErrors are in files they import; cost is YOUR import graph (leaf 2.6s, hub 63s), so a hub can time out. Either way ok/errorCount/errors/exitCode describe the requested files, otherErrorCount/otherErrors stay separate, and parser/global/partial-scope failures make scopedVerdict incomplete rather than green. ⚠ NARROWER GUARANTEE: neither sees every file your change can break (a transitive importer on the service, any non-importer on the CLI). For the gate verdict use the project-wide run or `npm run lint:tsc -- --files=...`.

command.description: The bash command to run (passed to `bash -c`). Required, unless `cmd` is given. For inline Python `-c`, do not encode source line breaks as literal `\n` inside a shell-quoted program: the shell preserves the backslash and Python raises a line-continuation SyntaxError. Use a quoted heredoc (`python3 - <<'PY' ... PY`) or a semicolon-delimited one-liner.

cmd.description: Alias for `command`. Accepted because the Codex CLI's own native `shell` tool call uses "cmd" as its argument key (EI-22073622160284651: a Codex-backed agent reaching for this tool by habit typed `cmd` and was rejected), so an agent used to that convention can reach for it here too. Prefer `command`.

description.description: 5–10 word description of what the command does (for telemetry / the agent log).

timeout.description: Wall-clock timeout in ms (minimum 1000; values below one second are rejected to catch seconds-vs-milliseconds mistakes — 20 seconds = 20000ms). This is the EXECUTION deadline, not the response window. Ordinary calls default to 120000; if still running at the response window they return the SAME durable job without killing it. Explicit run_in_background calls default to 14400000. Maximum 43200000. The whole confined task subtree IS terminated only at this execution deadline (systemd RuntimeMaxSec plus the local SIGTERM/SIGKILL path), so budget it for all command wall-clock work, including sleeps, SSH/remote round-trips, retries, and other waits; raise it when that planned work can run longer. The deadline is FIXED AT LAUNCH and cannot be extended on a running task (systemd 255 refuses a runtime RuntimeMaxSec change): size it for retries, or chain longer work as separate tasks. Deliberately daemonized descendants remain tracked inside the same task and share its deadline; use a dedicated service launcher for a different lifetime. Work submitted to an external server can outlive the shell: killing psql does not prove its PostgreSQL query stopped. Use dev:pg_query for bounded diagnostic reads, or set and verify a server-side statement_timeout for native SQL.

yield_after_ms.description: Ordinary-call RESPONSE window in ms (default 45000, max 45000). If the command is still running when this window ends, the call returns its original durable bash_id/task_id and the job continues until completion, explicit kill/abort, or the separate timeout execution deadline. This never restarts or duplicates the command. Ignored with run_in_background:true, which yields immediately.

run_in_background.description: Return the durable job immediately instead of waiting for fast completion. Ordinary calls already yield the same job automatically at yield_after_ms. Read later output via capability:bash_output.

require_task_confinement.description: Require managed task enrollment and cgroup confinement before fork. Refuse without starting the command if unavailable; timeout still bounds the whole task.

allow_duplicate.description: Allow a duplicate launch when a live task already has the exact same command and cwd. Use only when the duplicate is intentional.

cwd.description: Working dir (absolute, or relative to the project dir). Defaults to the project dir.

work_item_id.description: Held work-item this job is for. Required when you hold multiple work-items or held-item attribution cannot be measured; pass the exact full id returned by scheduler:get_next or work_items:get. Shortened or inferred ids are refused with the current held ids. Otherwise optional. Overrides your declared goal for task-ledger attribution and the slow-attempt loop gate.

parent_task_id.description: Durable task that owns this nested launch. Pass PAPERCUSP_CAPABILITY_BASH_BACKGROUND_TASK_ID from a managed caller. Must be live and owned by the same caller, workspace, harness and work-item; subtree cancellation then includes this child.

integration_env.description: Operator-authority only. Map child environment variable names to encrypted setup:save_integration_key names, e.g. {"DEEPGRAM_API_KEY":"SIDESTAGE_DEEPGRAM_API_KEY"}. Raw values stay server-side, exist only in this child process, and are exact-value-redacted from events, results, background reads, and spill logs.

tail.description: Return only the LAST N lines of the output text in THIS response (whichever of `output`/`output_tail` it carries — every response branch, including stranded/recovered ones, is covered). The read cursor still advances past the ENTIRE chunk regardless, exactly like `filter` — this only narrows what is RETURNED. Composes with `filter`: filter is applied first, then tail keeps the last N of what remains.

observe.description: How you want to SEE the result of this action. auto (default) = the accessibility tree when this desktop exposes one, else a screenshot. image = always a screenshot (~1049 tokens). tree = the tree or a loud refusal, never a silent screenshot. none = the one-line result only. The `screenshot` action always returns pixels regardless.

desktop.description: Which of your desktops to drive: a desktopSessionId or your own desktop's name (computer:list_desktops). Omit to use your only/most recently used desktop, else your pot's.

new_string.description: The replacement text (must differ from old_string).

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence (default false → require a unique match).

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL; required for HTTP fetch/browser navigation.

browser.description: Opt into a scoped Playwright browser: open/navigate/observe/close. Navigation and DOM reads only; remote writes, WebSockets, service workers, background network and downloads are refused. State is process-local; close/abort/idle expires it. Native TUI features remain enabled.

selector.description: CSS selector to wait for/observe; no arbitrary JavaScript.

screenshot.description: Return a bounded viewport PNG as an MCP image.

max_text_chars.description: DOM text character ceiling; default 10000. Result-door byte policy still applies.

body.description: Request body (string).

max_bytes.description: Max body bytes returned inline (default 100000, bounded by the shared 30000-byte inline ceiling); beyond the effective cap spills to a file.

max_download_bytes.description: Hard streamed response ceiling (default 52428800); the body is cancelled before further buffering or disk growth.

source.description: Local repository path (absolute, or relative to cwd). Defaults to cwd/project dir. Remote URLs are refused.

ref.description: Commit-ish to pin exactly and check out detached. Defaults to HEAD.

destination.description: Optional absolute, non-existing destination below OS temp or the source repository's ignored .papercusp/scratch directory on the source filesystem. Omit to create one safely.

submodules.description: Materialise locally checked-out submodules at their exact pins (default true). No network fallback.

scratchClone.description: Guarded, cheap, disposable local clone. Use instead of ad-hoc `git clone`/copy commands for scratch work.

role.description: The role to grant capabilities to (e.g. "planner", "cup").

check.description: typecheck = `npx tsc --noEmit` in the package; test = the package suite (`npx vitest run`), the repository `npm run test:file -- <path…>` router for exact one- or multi-file runs (including `.integration.test.*`, `.browser.test.*`, and `.e2e.test.*`), or, with no package and no paths, the repo `npm run test:affected`.

package.description: Repository-relative directory path to run in, e.g. "packages/operator-core", or the canonical npm workspace name such as "@papercusp/operator-core" (resolved via its node_modules workspace link). It must contain tsconfig.json for typecheck. For test, omit to run `npm run test:affected` at the repo root.

path.description: test only: one test file/dir to narrow the run (e.g. "lib/foo.test.ts"). When `package` is supplied, the path is package-relative; when omitted, it is repo-relative. Layered `.integration.test.*`/`.browser.test.*`/`.e2e.test.*` files are routed through the repository `test:file` command automatically. For multiple exact files, use `onlyPaths` instead; do not pass both fields.

onlyPaths.description: Exact paths for a focused run. For test, pass one or more package-relative paths (when `package` is supplied) or repo-relative paths (when omitted); they run through the root `npm run test:file -- <paths…>` router. For typecheck, discover the repository baseline gate that covers these package- or repo-relative paths, then scope its verdict via `--files=`. Mixed or uncovered gate scopes are refused rather than guessed.

run_in_background.description: Run detached; returns a bash_id immediately. Poll with capability:bash_output, stop with processes:kill { taskId }.

runInBackground.description: Compatibility alias for run_in_background; the snake_case spelling is canonical.

timeout.description: Wall-clock timeout in ms. FOREGROUND: default 120000, clamped to 45000ms (below the ~55s MCP transport cap) so it returns a hint instead of an opaque request_timeout. BACKGROUND (run_in_background): default 14400000, max 43200000 — not bound by the transport cap, but still terminated at its own deadline.

brief.description: First-turn request; REQUIRED for resume/fork except a guarded system:lineage-neutral-successor resume. Optional for fresh plan-bound or per-member briefs, or a successor with seeded carry. Delivery does not prove a turn started or claimed work; read launch verification.

plan.description: Plan slug to bind the agent to — it launches on the plan and auto-kicks-off against it (the fleet:launch-on-plan behavior, without needing a fleet).

harness.description: Harness slug to bootstrap for an operator-scope launch. Required when the caller context is wildcard/unset; otherwise the caller harness is used.

mcpTarget.description: 'spawn-host' binds bootstrap and MCP to this operator for a bounded current-build check; default 'stable' uses the proxy.

workItem.description: Exact work-item id that authorizes this launch under a work-scope exception (for example, the scorecard being independently audited).

feature.description: Work-item/feature id passed as psu --feature on a fresh launch. For an accepted-operation worker, it must equal workItem; resume and fork retain their source binding.

resume.description: Resume full context with a required non-empty brief, except a guarded system:lineage-neutral-successor resume for a dormant critical frozen-tests author. For ordinary in-place continuation, send `{ resume, brief }`. Add `fork:false` for strict in-place recovery that refuses a live source instead of auto-forking. Choose agentId (latest) OR sessionId (exact). Omitted settings use the target/saved fleet profile. Leave `carry` out because it is rejected for resume/fork. Normally omit `account` and `model` too; overrides may conflict with the saved fleet profile. Use successor for fresh context with retained identity and explicit runtime/carry.

agentId.description: The agent's coord id (e.g. 'su-a1a71' — a prefix is fine). Resolves its MOST-RECENT session automatically.

sessionId.description: An exact native CLI session uuid, when you want to pin one specific session rather than the agent's latest.

successor.description: Fresh context for an ENDED predecessor, preserving owner identity, claims and seeded recovery brief. Allows explicit fresh-context `account`, `model`, or `carry` settings. Visible by default when `headless` is omitted or `false`; headless:true hides the window. Cannot combine with restoreVisible. Live sources are refused; resume auto-forks them for a parallel branch.

agentId.description: The ended predecessor's coord id (e.g. 'su-a1a71' — a prefix is fine).

sessionId.description: The ended predecessor's exact native CLI session uuid.

successorLineageMode.description: Request the system lineage parent only for a dormant critical frozen-tests author recovered through `resume`. The handler requires an identity-preserving successor, verifies the exact non-terminal manifest author and independence, and rejects caller-authored prompt/profile overrides. Not valid for ordinary resume, fork, or explicit successor.

originalRouting.description: Repair the provider route of an exact quiescent Codex thread using its saved gateway account. Pin its original owner, adv row, UUID, isolated home and codexOriginalRoutingFingerprint. Requires an existing healthy profile/transcript; live or changed custody refuses, without fork, successor, shutdown or profile repair. Omit all runtime/settings overrides.

fork.description: Resume routing: omit this for the normal protective behavior (a LIVE source is automatically forked); `true` always branches to a FRESH identity; explicit `false` requires an in-place resume and fails closed if the source is LIVE, rather than silently changing to a fork.

restoreVisible.description: Recover an exact resume.sessionId after its desktop window disappeared. No surviving host: ordinary exact resume. A surviving host is shut down gracefully ONLY with kernel cgroup proof its window is dead; alive/unknown/non-window hosts are refused. For stale headless hosts omit this flag and use ordinary exact resume. Verify the restored visible terminal.

agent.description: Which agent CLI backs a FRESH launch (default: the psu default). For resume, an explicit different backend requests a session port that retains the source identity; supply a compatible model. Live-source resumes automatically fork, so they cannot cross backends. A fork keeps the recorded backend. An identity-preserving successor may explicitly override the predecessor backend.

role.description: psu --role: a registered persona id resolved against the target harness (the valid ids are harness-specific). Discover exact ids first with roles:list { harnessSlug: "<target>" } and read roles[].id; roles:known lists built-in ids. This is not a lane/job label; put lane direction in the brief or label.

stack.description: Repeatable psu --stack `<slot>:<id>` bindings (e.g. `domain:papercusp-engineer`) for every fresh launch; bare ids are invalid. members[i].stack overrides this list.

fleet.description: Fleet name or slug to JOIN (membership + the fleet's bound window colour). Optional: omit it and a FRESH launch falls back to YOUR OWN presence-fleet (WI-4234); a RESUME/FORK preserves the target session's latest durable fleet membership instead of inheriting the caller's fleet.

independent.description: Keep a FRESH launch out of the caller's presence fleet; an explicit `fleet` still wins (RESUME/FORK membership: see `fleet`).

goalVerifier.description: GOAL holder only: launch one independent GRADE or TEST session, bind its matching goal launch profile and mode before turn one, and couple the holder to the verifier.

headless.description: Launch with no window (logs to a file under the workspace fleet-logs dir) instead of a visible desktop terminal. Default false = visible. Headless sessions stay injectable (managed pty).

count.description: How many agents to launch with this brief/plan (default 1 — or the length of `members` when that is given). Every actual start is independently admitted by the durable resource governor. Not allowed with an in-place resume — one session cannot be resumed N times (fork it instead).

members.description: Index-aligned FRESH multi-launch config (entry 0 = agent 1). Set fields override top-level args, then system defaults. Registered roles only; invalid personas fail atomically before launch. Missing entries use flat args; omitted count uses members.length. Not for resume/fork. claimKinds requires a self-pulling fleet via fleet:launch-on-plan.

model.description: psu --model: this member's model spec, overriding the fleet `model`.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this member. Composed onto the model spec (`<model>:<effort>`) — psu has no separate --effort flag — so it REQUIRES a model (this member's or the fleet's).

contextSize.description: psu --context-size for this member (growable trimmed seed).

compactionLimit.description: psu --compaction-limit: this member's soft compaction limit in TOKENS (>= 20000). Clamped down to the fleet-role ceiling at seed time — it can lower a member's limit, never raise it past its cap.

role.description: psu --role: a registered persona id resolved against the target harness (the valid ids are harness-specific). Discover exact ids first with roles:list { harnessSlug: "<target>" } and read roles[].id; roles:known lists built-in ids. This is not a lane/job label; put lane direction in this member's `brief` or the shared `label`.

stack.description: Repeatable psu --stack `slot:id` bindings for this member. Replaces the fleet-wide `stack` when set.

agent.description: psu --agent (claude|omp|codex) for this member.

launchContext.description: psu --launch-context: this member's own brief FILE path.

brief.description: Inline brief TEXT for this member — becomes its own first turn / composed launch context. Use instead of `launchContext` when you have the text, not a file. Takes precedence over this member's `perMemberLaunchContext` entry.

claimKinds.description: Per-member claim lane — seeds THIS member's claim spec, overriding the fleet-level `claimKinds`.

display.description: Open this member's terminal on this X display.

extraArgs.description: Extra verbatim psu args for this member.

cwd.description: Working dir for a FRESH launch (absolute, or relative to the harness project dir). A resume always lands in the session's own recorded cwd.

label.description: Display label (shown in /adv/sessions + the window title).

display.description: WI-4272 (demo/recording): open the window(s) on this X display (e.g. ':110') instead of the owner's desktop seat. Linux + visible only.

account.description: Account routing for a fresh launch or successor: 'default' (the system login), 'auto' (gateway-routed), or a pool account id. Defaults to 'default' on every platform; the gateway is never selected implicitly. For ordinary in-place resume, omit it to use the target's recorded or saved-fleet account. An explicit resume override is intentional and may be refused if it conflicts with the saved fleet profile. Always resolved — a scripted launch must never block on the interactive account picker.

model.description: Model override for a fresh launch or successor (e.g. an opus/sonnet spec). For ordinary in-place resume, omit it to use the target session model; an explicit resume override is intentional and may be refused if it conflicts with the saved fleet profile.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for every member (low|medium|high|xhigh|max); members[].effort overrides it. Human model aliases resolve through config:tiers-get launchAliases.

extraArgs.description: Extra psu flags passed through as individually shell-quoted argv values (e.g. ['--brain', '--context-size=trimmed']) — the capability:terminal pass-through model, so a NEW psu flag or structured JSON value needs no tool change.

idempotencyKey.description: Dedupe key for retries: pass the SAME key when re-firing a call that may have already landed — a replay reports deduped:true (with what the original launched) instead of opening a SECOND set of agent windows.

carry.description: Warm/cold auto-mode carry for a FRESH launch or identity-preserving successor. `members[i].carry` overrides this flat value. Do not set it with in-place `resume`/`fork`: the schema rejects it and the target session's loop/profile carry is retained.

schema.x-papercusp-call-constraint: resume or fork => non-empty top-level brief required, except guarded system:lineage-neutral-successor resume

command.description: The command to run in this terminal (bash). Runs verbatim, then the terminal drops to an interactive shell.

cwd.description: Working dir for this terminal (absolute, or relative to the harness project dir).

label.description: Display label for this terminal (shown in /adv/sessions and the window title).

fleet.description: Optional fleet name or slug — every terminal in this call uses that fleet's permanently-bound color scheme, and any `psu` command in it auto-joins that fleet (--fleet=<slug> injected). When omitted, the tool automatically resolves your OWN presence-fleet (if you are a fleet member) for both color AND `psu` membership (WI-4234) — so a bare `psu ...` spawned by a fleet leader/member joins the caller's fleet by default. Pass an explicit `fleet` to OVERRIDE which fleet a spawned `psu` joins, or to color/join a fleet you are not currently a member of. Prefer `fleet:launch-on-plan` over hand-rolling a fleet spawn here when you can — it also seeds plan/launch-context.

display.description: WI-4272 (demo/recording): open EVERY terminal in this call on this X display (e.g. ':110' — a computer:provision_desktop sandbox stage being recorded) instead of the owner's desktop seat. Linux only; requires a DISPLAY-honoring emulator (xterm/alacritty/kitty/wezterm) and the display's X socket to be alive (loud-fail otherwise). Omit for normal visible-desktop use.

file_path.description: Absolute path, or relative to the project dir.

content.description: Full file content to write (overwrites any existing file).

allow_empty_overwrite.description: Permit empty content to replace an existing non-empty file (deliberate truncation). Without it that one case is refused.

allow_display_formatted_content.description: Permit content that looks like capability:read's line-numbered display view (normally a sign the text should have come from raw:true).

id.description: Fetch one entry by catalog id (e.g. 'ornith-35b-iq3m-llama-server'). Omit for the full catalog.

backendId.description: A registered local-backend id (gateway:local_backend_list) — resolves baseUrl + backend kind. Mutually exclusive with baseUrl/backend.

baseUrl.description: Explicit backend root, e.g. 'http://127.0.0.1:11436' (no trailing /v1). Use with `backend` when the target isn't registered.

backend.description: Serving engine kind — required when `baseUrl` is given instead of `backendId`.

model.description: The OpenAI /v1 model id the backend serves, e.g. 'maxwell1500/ornith-35b:IQ3_M'.

quant.description: Quantization label for the report's config, e.g. 'IQ3_M' or 'awq'. Default 'unknown' (descriptive only — does not reconfigure the backend).

numCtx.description: TOTAL context across all parallel slots, for the report's config (descriptive only). Default 0 (unknown).

parallel.description: Parallel slots, for the report's config (descriptive only). Default 1.

apiKey.description: Optional bearer token (local backends typically need none).

workspace.description: Workspace id (default: ctx / active workspace) — used to resolve `backendId`.
workspace to inspect (default: the session/active workspace)

limit.description: max rows (default 50)

sinceHours.description: only rows recorded in the trailing N hours

workspace.description: workspace to inspect (default: the session/active workspace)

decision.description: Decision-context for the autonomy gate (B-17/P-040) — only the cup self-answer path uses it; omit for ordinary human-facing questions.

action.description: Tool/verb or short slug of the action the decision is about (maps to an autonomy category, B-04).

addressee.description: Where these addresses came from. "contact" (with a personal:search contact externalId) and "thread-participant" are VERIFIED server-side; "owner-instruction" means the owner named it directly and is accepted only if the address is not one that appears solely in message content.

pipeline.description: Scope to ONE pipeline's gate — the repo basename of its integration root (e.g. 'papercusp'). Omit to default to the current dev pipeline, unless runId is supplied (then global keys are filtered to that exact run). Use global:true for the global keys, which wake on EVERY co-hosted pipeline's verdict (EI-7646: you then must lineage-check payload.sha/payload.pipeline yourself).

candidateSha.description: EI-12457: bind the wait to this exact candidate (full sha or a prefix) via a payload predicate on the emitted payload.sha — a verdict for any OTHER candidate (a stale/superseded run) will NOT wake you; you keep sleeping until the correct candidate resolves or the deadline. Strongly recommended whenever you know which commit you are judging (e.g. right after a git-sync:await/deploy). WI-5685: this is an EXACT match, not an ancestry check — a LATER candidate that still contains your commit (e.g. the hourly cron races ahead and judges a newer tip) will NOT wake you even though its green verdict already covers you. If a cron tick could plausibly land before your exact candidate does, omit candidateSha (wake on ANY verdict for this pipeline) and confirm inclusion afterwards with release:trace instead of binding here. EI-18676650746298156: if this EXACT candidate was already judged before you armed (recorded in harness_shared.pipeline_events), you get already_judged:true immediately instead of sleeping to the timeout — this is the same EXACT-match rule as above, so it can never be fooled by a later candidate that merely contains your commit.

runId.description: WI-4957: bind further to the EXACT run (payload.runId, an exact match) that judged your candidate — only needed when two runs might judge the SAME candidate sha (a re-fire, or a routine/manual race) and you must not accept the other one's verdict. With no explicit pipeline, runId uses the global event keys so the exact run can be awaited across co-hosted installs. Combines with candidateSha (both must match); rarely needed on its own.

global.description: Use the global release:green / green-checkpoint:red keys instead of the current pipeline's keys. Only for cross-pipeline monitors.

note.description: Why you are waiting — echoed into the wake turn.

timeout_sec.description: Deadline in seconds (0 = bounded immediate probe; default 11400 ≈ 190min — WI-5685: sized to the suite's real worst-case ceiling, the 180min systemd backstop + slack, NOT the generic events:await default (1800s) which used to strand a default-timeout caller mid-suite); on the deadline you are woken with a TIMEOUT marker.

on_timeout.description: What happens at the deadline without the event: 'wake' (default) = re-invoke with a TIMEOUT marker; 'expire' = lapse silently (visible in events:status).

claimId.description: The claim id — a checks[] row `id`, or the `<id>` of a `claim:<id>` mention. A leading `claim:`/`#` is stripped.

because.description: Why the claim is wrong (or, with reinstate, why the retraction was wrong). Shown beside the ⛔ marker.

supersededBy.description: What replaces it — a work-item id, a claim id, or a short pointer to the corrected conclusion.

reinstate.description: Reverse a prior retraction (the claim stands again). Refused when the claim is not currently retracted.

remove.description: Tool names to REMOVE from the scoped-SU cross-workspace allowlist.

id.description: Namespaced job-scoped class id, e.g. crm.email or storage.object-read.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema for the class verb input.

outputSchema.description: Optional JSON Schema for the class verb structured output.

behavioralSuiteRef.description: Optional future behavioral-suite hook. P-016 structural validation reports it as not-run, never passed.

ref.description: Exact class ref, e.g. crm.email@1.0.0.

includeVersions.description: Return all matching versions instead of only the newest per class id.

providerPackage.description: Projected-tool plugin/package owner, matched exactly against tool.pluginName.

verbBindings.description: Logical class verb → actual MCP tool name.

op.description: pack = the matching files (Repomix). diff = what changed (code2prompt). Neither writes.

include.description: REQUIRED glob set, e.g. ["packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/**"]. A pattern starting with "-" is refused.

ignore.description: Extra excludes. Appended to a non-overridable secret deny-set (.env, keys, credentials), never replacing it.

format.description: Document format. Defaults to xml for pack, markdown for diff.

template.description: Prepend a reviewer framing: code-review | security-audit | refactor-prep | none.

baseRef.description: diff only: ref to diff against, e.g. "origin/main". Omitted = the working-tree diff.

compress.description: pack only: collapse bodies to signatures. Much smaller; loses implementation detail.

rootPath.description: Project root override. Defaults to the agent workspace root.

explain.description: diff only: bounded native change report with current compiler consumers, tests, source/runtime provenance, ownership and freshness. Re-submit previousFingerprint before editing or reviewing.

kernel.description: Opt into a live JavaScript worker/VM: open creates an owner/workspace/harness-scoped id, run executes a cell, status inspects it, close cancels and cleans it up. Use globalThis for cross-cell objects/functions/binary state; lexical locals remain cell-local. Each cell dispatches with CURRENT caller authority. No Python kernel, implicit lexical-declaration persistence, or process-restart recovery is claimed. Timeout/cancel loses state; idle expires after 5 minutes. Persistent kernels are refused on volatile staging :3170 because its process is recycled frequently. For restart-safe work, call store(key,value), persist the returned state, and pass it back through inputs on the next stateless or kernel call. Dry-run kernel operations are refused because VM state mutations cannot be previewed safely.

inputs.description: Explicit JSON-only replay state for the sandbox inputs object. Use with store/load: a successful run returns state when store/load was used; persist that state outside the process and pass it here after an operator restart. Inputs never restore arbitrary globalThis objects or functions.

work_item_id.description: Default work-item attribution for nested capability:bash calls. Use the exact held WI-/EI-/F- id when this session holds multiple work-items; an explicit nested work_item_id takes precedence.

script.description: Plain JavaScript body only (TypeScript annotations such as `: any` are not supported). Call tools via `await tools.ns.verb(args)`; `return` a compact summary. There is no tools.invoke shortcut in this sandbox; dynamic dispatch is tools.tools.invoke({ name, args }), or use tools.ns.verb(args) directly. The recursive execution doors `tools.code.run` and `tools.orchestrate.run` are deliberately excluded from this facade; keep the sequence in this outer script. On script timeout, `timeoutSettledReadRecovery.calls` returns settled read-only child results, capped at 24 KiB/20 calls; check `omittedReadCount`, and never assume a slow Promise.all sibling returned to the script. A timeout with settled work is marked `partial:true` in the public envelope; use the last recovered page's cursor/hash to resume without replaying settled reads. Write results are never included in timeout recovery. No ambient `exec`/shell helper exists -- `tools` exposes ONLY `tools.ns.verb(args)` calls; To run a shell command, call `tools.capability.bash({ command })` like any other tool. If you hold multiple work-items, pass `work_item_id` naming a work-item you currently hold: `await tools.capability.bash({ command, work_item_id: "WI-1234" })`. Omission returns `work_item_id_required` before dispatch; a single held claim can remain implicit. Nested tool calls return their typed result root, not an MCP `content`/`text` envelope: for example, read `result.output`, `result.exit_code`, and `result.status` from capability:bash; do not read `result.content[0].text`. For `dev:pg_query`, query results expose `result.rows`, `result.fields`, and `result.rowCount`; relation descriptions expose `result.columns`, `result.indexes`, and `result.constraints`. To emit final media, return exactly `{ summary, media: [{ type: "image"|"audio", data: "<base64>", mimeType }] }`; media from intermediate tool calls is never emitted implicitly. Compatibility helpers are ambient: `notify(value)` and `yield_control()` stream through the current transport; `generatedImage({ image_url: "data:image/...;base64,...", output_hint? })` appends a validated image; `store(key, value)` / `load(key)` use explicit replay state seeded from bindings/inputs and returned with the result -- never hidden session memory. Replay state is capped at 200 keys and 65,536 UTF-8 bytes (64 KiB); `store` rejects larger state with `state_limit_exceeded` instead of truncating it. Keep replay state to compact cursors, IDs, and bounded summaries: reduce large tool reads at the source with `projection.pick`, `limit`, or checkpoint pages, and use `payloadTier:'full'` only with a narrow projection. For exact oversized returns, follow `summaryNotice.rawSummaryCursor` with `capability:read`; split recovery into bounded slices instead of storing the whole envelope, then pass the compact state through `inputs`. No setTimeout or setInterval usage -- neither is ambient in this sandbox -- use `await sleep(ms)` for a short bounded delay (e.g. write-then-reverify) instead. sleep() caps at 10s and returns the actual ms waited -- use that (not ms) when measuring a window, e.g. a rate over a delta. A shell-command STRING passed to `tools.capability.bash({ command })` needs JS escaping too: write `tr '\\0' ' ' </proc/self/cmdline` (two backslashes in the script source); a single `\0` JS escape becomes a NUL and is rejected before bash runs. Literal shell backslashes need the same JS escaping: use String.raw for the script or double each backslash in a JS string, e.g. `find /tmp \\( -name '*.unlikely-no-match' \\)`; a single `\(` becomes `(` before bash runs, breaking grouped predicates. Shell parameter expansion needs the same template-layer escape: inside a JavaScript template literal, write `\${f##*/}` (or avoid the expansion) so the JavaScript compiler does not treat the shell `${f##*/}` as its own template expression; otherwise code:run returns `compile_error` before bash is dispatched. Multiline shell commands need the JavaScript string layer too: use a backtick template literal for `command` when it contains literal newlines, or escape each line break as `\n`; a literal newline inside a single/double-quoted string causes `compile_error` before bash dispatch. Regex literals containing path slashes are another string layer: an extra backslash before `/` can close the literal early and yield `compile_error: Invalid regular expression flags`; prefer `String.includes(...)` or `new RegExp("...")` when composing scripts through another string layer. Generated data needs the same JS layer: do not interpolate `JSON.stringify(ids)` into a JavaScript double-quoted command literal. Nested tools.capability.bash searches: apostrophe regexes break single-quoted arguments; use rg -F, -e per pattern, or quoted stdin/file. The JSON quotes can close that outer string and cause `compile_error` before bash is dispatched; keep the serialized value in a script variable and concatenate it into the command at runtime (or pass it through quoted stdin, a heredoc, or an argument). For inline Python `-c`, put the shell command in a JavaScript template literal and the Python program in single quotes, e.g. ``const command = String.raw`journalctl -u app.service | python3 -c 'import sys; print("ts", sys.stdin.readline().strip())'`;``. This keeps Python's quotes from closing a JavaScript double-quoted command and prevents `compile_error` before bash is dispatched. Do not encode Python source line breaks as literal `\n` inside the shell-quoted program: the shell preserves the backslash and Python raises a line-continuation SyntaxError. Use a quoted heredoc (`python3 - <<'PY' ... PY`) or a semicolon-delimited one-liner.

title.description: Short title for the reusable RECIPE saved on a successful run — make it discoverable by other agents (e.g. "triage stale work-items"). Optional: a fallback is derived from the script when omitted.

description.description: One/two lines on what this recipe does + when to reuse it. Optional: derived from the tool-set when omitted.

dryRun.description: Preview: record effect:write tool calls without executing them (reads still run).

timeoutSec.description: Wall-clock budget (default 30s). EFFECTIVE CEILING IS 45s. EI-9239: code:run has no run_in_background — every call is foreground, and the papercusp-su MCP transport hard-caps a foreground call at ~55s. Values above 45s are rejected by the input schema; the runtime clamp remains a defense for internal callers that bypass transport validation. For work that genuinely needs longer, split it into multiple code:run calls or fall back to individual tool calls.

op.description: search lists matches; rewrite_preview reports replacements; syntax_index emits inferred declarations; taint evaluates declared local data flow separately using Semgrep OSS. All are read-only.

pattern.description: Structural pattern: code with metavariables. `$X` is one node, `$$$X` is many.

language.description: Grammar to parse the pattern and files with. A pattern is only meaningful under a language.

rewrite.description: rewrite_preview only: replacement template, reusing the pattern's metavariables. NOTHING is written.

taint.description: taint only: explicit source, sink and optional sanitizer patterns. No implicit security model or inter-file completeness claim.

paths.description: Search/rewrite files or directories; defaults to workspace root. syntax_index requires 1..16 explicit source files, each at most 1 MiB; generated/vendor source is excluded.

rootPath.description: Project root override. Defaults to the agent workspace root.

limit.description: Cap on returned sites. A cut is always reported via truncation.truncated + totalAvailable.

namespaces.description: Render full signatures for just these namespaces (e.g. ["work_items","coord"]).

names.description: Render signatures for these exact tool names (e.g. ["plans:set-status"]). Union with namespaces.

ref.description: The #ref of the element, exactly as computer:observe printed it (e.g. "0/0/2/1").

action.description: Which of the element's actions to fire (default: its first). computer:observe does not list these; omit unless a previous error named one.

desktop.description: Which of your desktops to drive: a desktopSessionId or your own desktop's name (computer:list_desktops). Omit to use your only/most recently used desktop, else your pot's.

filter.description: "mine" = your own desktops, "pot" = your pot's shared desktop, "all" (default) = every desktop in the workspace.

include_hidden.description: Include elements the toolkit reports as not on screen (e.g. unopened menus). Default false.

include_bounds.description: Include each element's on-screen box. Default false — you click by #ref, not by coordinate.

desktop.description: Which of your desktops to drive: a desktopSessionId or your own desktop's name (computer:list_desktops). Omit to use your only/most recently used desktop, else your pot's.

pot.description: Equip this pot (home-harness slug) with its ONE shared desktop. Omit to start a desktop for yourself.

name.description: Name of YOUR desktop (default desktop-<n>). Re-using a name returns that desktop.

apps.description: GUI apps to launch on the desktop, each an argv array — e.g. [["firefox","--no-remote"],["soffice","--calc"]].

width.description: Screen width in px (default 1024 — best computer-use grounding).

capture_width.description: Px width the AGENT is served (default 1024); the screen still runs at `width`.

capture_height.description: Px height the AGENT is served (default 768). Larger costs proportionally more tokens.

op.description: start a recording, stop it, report the open one, or render one to video.

workItem.description: Work-item this recording belongs to (e.g. "WI-1234"). Bound at `start`; `export` parks its pointer comment there.

note.description: Short human note stored in the manifest ("reproducing the save-dialog hang").

desktop.description: Which of your desktops to drive: a desktopSessionId or your own desktop's name (computer:list_desktops). Omit to use your only/most recently used desktop, else your pot's.

format.description: export format (default webm; gif for pasting into a thread).

recording.description: export a SPECIFIC recording id (default: this display's open recording, else the most recent).

maxFrames.description: frame files kept on disk (default 240); the oldest are evicted past it.

maxDurationSec.description: wall-clock ceiling; crossing it auto-stops the recording (default 3600s).

desktop.description: The desktop to release: its desktopSessionId, or the name of one of your own desktops.

pot.description: Release this pot's shared desktop; requires pot-management authority.

doorSplit.description: All-or-nothing; output + resultSlots×resultEach + injections must equal 1.

clear.description: Drop this session’s override (ignores the other fields).

dryRun.description: Preview the mutation without applying it.

maxTurnCapTokens.description: Per-hop budget cap (baked 15000). Must stay ≥ the effective floor.

doorSplit.description: All-or-nothing; output + resultSlots×resultEach + injections must equal 1.

compactionOverheadTokens.description: Fixed per-hop overhead reserve in the threshold math (baked 4000).

clear.description: Wipe the workspace layer back to baked (ignores the other fields).

dryRun.description: Preview the mutation without applying it.

concern.description: Limit to one concern by name; omit for all.
Concern name to reset; omit and pass all:true to reset every concern.

all.description: Reset ALL registered concerns to defaults.

dryRun.description: Preview what would reset without applying.

roles.description: Resolve these roles specifically. Omit to report the configured roles.

limit.description: Soft compaction limit in tokens. Requests above the target session's model-and-role ceiling return ok:false with the ceiling and make no write; in-range requests persist verbatim.

ownerId.description: P-006: the TARGET session to set (default: yourself). Setting ANOTHER session requires you to be the recorded leader of ITS fleet (or the queen / owner) — requests above THAT session's model + fleet-role ceiling are rejected with no write. Use to set a member's limit directly instead of asking it to.

name.description: Tier name (short, lowercase — the cup:spawn `tier` key).

backend.description: Backend override for this tier; absent = inherit the host backend.

when.description: One-line guidance: when an agent should pick this tier.

compactionLimit.description: Soft compaction limit (tokens) sessions on this tier are seeded with. Omit for the tier default. Clamped to [20k, that default] — floor((window − 10k) / 1.2), capped by the role cost cap where one binds (400k on [1m]).

tiers.description: The FULL replacement menu, ordered weakest → strongest. [] reverts to the committed defaults.

outcome.description: 'answered' = structured answer below; 'cant_help' = honest can't-help with reason; 'graduate' = the consult outgrew its bounds (D-004) — mints a shared work item, requires reason.

evidence.description: Transcript grounding [{ session_id, turn_idx, note? }] — an ARRAY of transcript-turn tuples, never prose or tool-probe output. If your evidence is not a transcript turn, OMIT this field; never fabricate session_id/turn_idx.

reason.description: Why (required for outcome=cant_help and outcome=graduate — for graduate: why the question outgrew the consult).
Why your context does not cover it (e.g. 'my transcript touches the file but not this subsystem').

request_key.description: Stable retry identity scoped to your workspace and requester. Reuse with the same question/options after a timeout. A different payload under the same key refuses; use a new key for a fresh consult. Omitted keys deduplicate identical requests.

question.description: The new question to route. This tool opens a new consult; to read an existing conversation, use conversations:get { id }. Name concrete files/symbols where relevant — authorship of the code in question is a routing signal.

subject_refs.description: Source refs whose transcript evidence must each support floor qualification. Public manual document paths expand through their documents: frontmatter anchors; unresolved or unmeasured anchors stay below the floor. There is no per-array count cap.

tried.description: What you already tried (grounds the responder; avoids re-suggesting it).

decision_at_stake.description: The decision this consult informs — the requester owns it (advice, not consensus).

latency_contract.description: 'proceed' (default): continue on your own judgment and use relevant advice when it arrives. 'hard-blocked': you will park on the returned park_key event.

origin_task_ref.description: Work-item/task this consult is attributed to (default: your most recently progressed wip work-item).

exclude.description: Owners to exclude from candidacy — e.g. the exhausted menu's decliners when re-routing after a terminal 'declined'/'expired' (the cascade itself advances server-side; no per-decline re-call).

parent_consult_id.description: Consulting onward from WITHIN a consult you are answering? Pass THAT consult's conversation_id: depth = parent+1 (capped at 2), and the lineage's participants are excluded from routing (cycle refusal, D-005).

max_agents.description: Cap on the selected cascade menu (default 3). Delivery stays single-dispatch: only the top selectee gets an isolated answer session, the rest are the menu (remaining_candidates).

min_agents.description: Select at least this many responders even below the relevance floor (best-available LIVE fill, labeled via:'minimum'; default 1). Pass 0 to restore pure-floor selection.

policy.description: Named selection policy to take min/max from ('rubric-vetting' for the meta-rubric vetting consult). Prefer this over typing max_agents at a governed call site — the bound then lives in code, not in your instructions. Unknown key refuses.

reviewerModel.description: For policy:'rubric-vetting': preserve this allowed backend/model/effort through every reviewer dispatch; unavailable choices refuse without substitution. Provider accounts use auto routing.

archive_floor.description: Similarity floor for the archive-first serve (default ~0.8, precision-biased). Pass 2 to bypass the archive entirely (force fresh routing — e.g. when an archived answer did not fit your context); lower it only when a stale-but-close answer beats waking anyone.

allow_dispatch.description: Allow launching an answering session from the matched expert (fork same-backend, convert cross-backend; default true). Pass false to keep this consult retrieval-only — you get the ranked candidates and read their transcripts yourself.

topics.description: Area topics to tag the consult with (ambient discoverability).

harness.description: Tag the conversation harness-scoped.

conversation_id.description: The consult conversation (from the wake / get_feedback result).

kind.description: Responder: answer | clarifying_question | new_fact. Requester follow-up: question | new_fact.

evidence.description: Transcript grounding [{ session_id, turn_idx, note? }] — REQUIRED for kind=answer (D-004).

stance.description: Decision-review consults (a parked product decision) ONLY, and REQUIRED there on every reviewer reply: support | no-view, or object with basis 'alternative' (reason + alternative), 'hazard' (reason + evidence refs) or 'owner-authority' (topic).

parkResponse.description: Parked agent (requester of a decision review) ONLY: answer an objection — adopt (take the alternative) or rebut (keep your default, with reasoning). Omitting objectionId answers the latest standing objection.

hours.description: Window length ending at `until` (default 24). Ignored when `since` is given.

since.description: Window start, ISO-8601. Launches at or after it count.

until.description: Window end, ISO-8601 (default now). Launches before it count.

about.description: What you are about to do, in a sentence. Ranks declared conventions and SELECTS which plan decisions are relevant. Omit to get declared conventions only — with nothing to rank against, arbitrary plan decisions would be noise dressed as governance.

harness.description: Harness whose plan decisions to search (default: your session harness). `'*'` — which is what a workspace-scoped session resolves to — searches EVERY harness in the workspace rather than a harness named `*`.

scopeRefs.description: Restrict role/owner/harness/work_item-scoped conventions to these refs. Workspace-scoped conventions are unconditional and always included. Default: your own owner id + harness.

limit.description: Max conventions returned (default 20).

full.description: Return COMPLETE bodies instead of excerpts. Default false.

role.description: Who said it — 'user' (the app user) or 'assistant' (you).

source.description: How it was conveyed; defaults to voice_stt for user, voice_tts for assistant.

limit.description: How many recent turns to return (default 20).

id.description: single-answer shorthand: the conversation id

body.description: the answer text applied to the inline id / every id in `ids`

mentions.description: owner ids to @-mention; applies to the inline id / every id in `ids`

ids.description: answer MANY conversations with the same `body` (homogeneous)

items.description: answer many conversations at once — each { id, body, mentions? }

id.description: conversation id (alias: conversation_id)

body.description: the answer text for THIS conversation

id.description: a single conversation id (n=1 shorthand for ids:[id])

conversation_id.description: alias for id (single form); id wins when both are supplied

id.description: single-join shorthand: the conversation id

mode.description: delivery mode for the inline id / every id in `ids`

ttl_sec.description: TTL for the inline id / every id in `ids`

leave.description: stop following the inline id / every id in `ids`

ids.description: join/leave MANY conversations with the same mode/leave (homogeneous)

items.description: join many conversations at once — each { id, mode?, ttl_sec?, leave? }

id.description: conversation id (alias: conversation_id)

harness.description: Restrict to a harness-scoped conversation set.

topic.description: Restrict to conversations tagged with this topic slug.

unansweredOnly.description: Only conversations with ZERO replies — the set that is still waiting on someone. Pair with kind:"question", state:"open" for "what can I answer right now".

includeUnscoped.description: With `harness`: ALSO include workspace-wide (operator-scope, harness-less) conversations instead of only that harness's. Most open questions here are workspace-wide, so a strict harness filter hides them.

conversation_id.description: Append to this conversation. Omit to start a new discussion.

id.description: Alias for conversation_id; conversation_id wins when both are supplied.

title.description: Short headline (new discussion only).

topics.description: Topic slugs to route a new discussion (new discussion only).

harness.description: Scope a new discussion to a harness (new discussion only).

id.description: single-promote shorthand: the conversation id

severity.description: Issue severity (default minor); applies to the inline id / every id in `ids`.
