timeout_s.description: Seconds to poll for the owner's answer before returning (default 0 — return immediately once the question is opened; conversation_id lets you check back later or events:await on conversation:answered:<conversation_id>). Only pass a positive value from an INTERACTIVE (non-code:run) session where you genuinely want this call to block — a foreground code:run script has an ~55s hard cap and WILL script_timeout if this polls anywhere near it.

supersedes_conversation_id.description: When correcting an existing owner ask, pass its conversation_id so the old gate is retracted and this replacement is opened durably.

note.description: Why you are idle / what you are waiting for — echoed into the wake turn. Auto-truncated to 2000 chars if longer.

min_sleep_sec.description: Per-subscriber wake floor: never re-wake within this window; a burst of sends inside it coalesces into ONE wake. Default: a sane standing floor.

plan_run_id.description: If you are a plan run, the wake resumes the run via plans:resume instead of a session resume.

audience.description: The audience selector to catch up on, e.g. @fleet:backend, @topic:federation, @plan:my-plan, or * (broadcast). Fleet names are slugified to match how they were stored.

limit.description: Max messages (newest kept). Default 50, max 500. Paginate older with before_ts/next_cursor.

token_budget.description: Accumulate messages newest-first until ~this many tokens, then stop (≥1 always returned). The "as much history as fits in my context" knob — right for a long backlog. Composes with limit: stops at whichever is hit first.

since_ts.description: Only messages strictly later than this ISO timestamp.

before_ts.description: Timestamp half of the pagination cursor; pass back next_cursor together with next_cursor_msg_id for the next older page.

before_msg_id.description: Message-id tie-breaker for before_ts; pass back next_cursor_msg_id so same-timestamp siblings are neither dropped nor repeated.

include_resolved.description: Also return resolved conditions (default true, capped by resolved_limit). Pass false for open-only.

resolved_limit.description: Max resolved conditions returned (most recent kept). Default 10.

condition_key.description: Exact condition key to read. Uses the keyed lifecycle lookup and returns only that condition; an unmatched key is reported with condition_found:false.

a.description: First agent — an ownerId, or "self". Defaults to you, so the common call is just { b }.

reason.description: Why they are coupled, for whoever finds the edge later ("both editing sync-resolver").

ttlSec.description: Expire the coupling after this many seconds. Omit for no TTL — it stands until someone decouples.

intent.description: One line: what you are working on right now.

current_plan_slug.description: Plan slug this work belongs to, if any; null is treated like omission.

items.description: P-NNN plan items you are taking (your LANE) — each is auto-claimed; your other claims in this plan are released. A non-empty lane requires current_plan_slug. Pass [] with a plan to release your whole lane; pass [] without a plan for a replacement-member presence re-declaration that does not touch plan claims. Omit to leave claims untouched. WI-/EI- work-item ids belong to scheduler:get_next, not this field.

declared_goal_refs.description: Optional typed goal refs explicitly covered by this declaration — generated goal slugs and WI-/EI- work-item refs are accepted; blank and bare numeric refs are rejected. Omit when no multi-goal declaration is intended; prose is never inferred.

harness.description: Harness the plan lives in, for the item claims (default: session harness, or operator home if unscoped).

current_files.description: Repo-relative files currently in scope — read by lock-contention enrichment (is the holder still focused on this path?) and by fleet placement. Omit to leave your declared file set untouched; pass [] to clear it. Same omission semantics as `items`.

ambient_excluded_refs.description: Work-item/session refs that ambient corpus retrieval must never inject into this session. Omit to preserve the durable fence; pass [] to clear it. A read failure fails closed for corpus retrieval.

a.description: First agent — an ownerId, or "self". Defaults to you, so the common call is just { b }.

reason.description: Why they were decoupled, for whoever finds the suppression later ("shared work shipped").

ttlSec.description: Lift the suppression automatically after this many seconds. Omit for a standing decoupling.

to.description: The target agent — its ownerId or the short handle from [coord+N]/coord:presence. Single-target only (never "*").

note.description: The directed instruction the target reads in its inbox on waking — what to pick up and do. Name the plan + items explicitly. coord:send delivers over-cap text as ordered inbox-sized parts and keeps the required wake on the final part.

planSlug.description: Plan slug whose items form the lane to assign (with `items`).

items.description: Plan-item ids (P-NNN) to push-assign to `to` as its durable lane. Omit for a pure directed wake.

workItemIds.description: Concrete promoted work-item ids to assign to the stable target. Re-read through canonical readiness; only actionable ids are claimed and included in the required wake. Mutually exclusive with `items`.

body.description: Optional body for the inbox note. coord:send delivers over-cap text as ordered inbox-sized parts; content beyond its chunk limit is refused with a durable-surface pointer.

harness.description: Harness scope for the lane assignment (default: the plan's harness).

resumeAdmission.description: Resume one exact existing work item through its active durable admission promoter, then assignment/wake. Requires harness and one workItemId. No replacement item is created; queued never means picked up.

pilotBinding.description: directed-pair pilot only: link the delivered role/session to a canonical binding receipt

summary.description: One-line summary of the escalation — auto-truncated to 2000 chars if longer.

conditionKey.description: Stable identifier for a RECURRING condition (e.g. "mug-placement-stall", "work-feed-dead"). Re-escalating the same conditionKey COALESCES onto the existing open row (bumps its repeatCount) instead of opening a new one; the response reports coalesced:true and bodyDiscarded:true when the new text is not persisted. Pass it for any watchdog/monitor condition you re-check on a cadence — especially when the summary embeds a live count or duration ("stalled ~7h", "302 items"), because without it the dedup falls back to the prose summary, which never repeats, and every wake leaks a new permanently-open escalation.

predicate.description: Optional machine-checkable condition for this escalation. Shape: { tool, args?, path, op, value? }, using the same read-only predicate contract as watch:create. It is checked now and re-checked before any SLA reroute; unreadable or missing state is stamped unknown and never treated as a contradiction.

options.description: Optional named choices the human can pick from. Omit for free-form.

evidence.description: How this escalation is GROUNDED: observed (you saw it) | tool-output (a tool result backs it; pass `ref`) | reported-by (a peer told you; `reportedBy` REQUIRED) | inferred (reasoned, not witnessed) | assumed (working assumption). Confidence is DERIVED from the band and rendered for the reader — never pass a number, it is discarded and flagged.

msg_id.description: Read exactly one known escalation by msg_id. Required for judge callers; cannot be combined with list filters.

offset.description: Page offset into the true open set (status=open only) — 0 for the first page, then +maxRecords each call, until truncated:false. No effect for status=resolved / unfiltered reads.

conditionKey.description: EI-15377: exact match against the record subjectSignature. See returns for match-completeness caveats.

q.description: EI-15377: case-insensitive substring match over summary+body. See returns for match-completeness caveats.

kinds.description: Restrict to these envelope kinds. Omitted = every kind.

owner.description: An ownerId. Matches envelopes where this owner is the sender OR a recipient; broadcasts match any owner.

from.description: Match the SENDER only (from === this ownerId). Unlike `owner`, does NOT match recipients and does NOT let broadcasts through — the precise "only what agent X SENT" filter (e.g. verify your own coord:send landed, or read one peer's messages).

audience.description: Restrict to envelopes addressed to this audience selector (@fleet:<slug> / @topic:<slug> / @plan:<slug> / @object:… / @file:… / *) — the audience-keyed HISTORY read. Catches up on everything sent to a fleet/topic even though your id was never in the resolved recipient list. (Members use coord:catch-up for the low-tier, membership-checked version.)

fleet.description: Compatibility alias for audience: a fleet slug or human name, normalized to @fleet:<slug>. If both fleet and audience are supplied, audience wins.

since.description: Preferred strictly-later-than ISO timestamp (older bound). Use this instead of legacy since_ts.

since_ts.description: Strictly later than this ISO timestamp (older bound).

before_ts.description: Timestamp half of the pagination cursor; pass back the returned next_cursor together with next_cursor_msg_id.

before_msg_id.description: Message-id tie-breaker for before_ts; pass back next_cursor_msg_id so same-timestamp siblings are neither dropped nor repeated.

limit.description: Max rows (newest kept). Agent default 30 (kept small because each row is a full envelope), max 500. Per-row body/summary are excerpted (body_truncated/_full_chars); paginate with before_ts/next_cursor for more.

token_budget.description: Accumulate rows newest-first until ~this many tokens, then stop (≥1 row always returned). The "as much history as fits in my context" knob — useful for a long backlog where a row count is hard to guess. Composes with limit: stops at whichever is hit first.

include_retracted.description: Also show messages withdrawn via coord:retract (default false — retracted messages are suppressed from the feed; the retraction notice itself is always visible). The forensic/audit escape hatch; coord:thread shows both without a flag.

ownerId.description: Exact coordination ownerId from coord:presence or fleet:assignments.

workspace.description: current brings here on Linux or when Windows permits the move; window switches to its workspace. Default: current on Linux, window on Windows/macOS.

audience.description: Who is looking — scopes which tips apply. Default 'user' (a human status surface).

state.description: Free-form caller state pairs for tip rules to match on (e.g. view=fleet-tab).

activity_limit.description: Recent activity rows to include (default 12; 0 to skip).

display_only.description: For human status surfaces that only print display.title/statusline/notice: compute display normally, but omit raw activity rows from the returned payload.

ownerId.description: The agent to ask about. Omit for your own goal.

accept_msg_id.description: Pass to accept an existing handoff; takes precedence over the open-handoff fields.

items.description: WI-4165: plan-item ids (P-NNN) of `plan_slug` handed off with this note — each one's own body is inlined into the delivered `body`, bounded, so the receiver reads WHAT to pick up without re-fetching the plan.

note.description: Free-form note when accepting.

schema.x-papercusp-call-constraint: unless accept_msg_id is nonempty (accept takes precedence): open-handoff requires to[], summary; plan_slug is optional for ad-hoc handoffs

from.description: Restrict to entries SENT BY this ownerId (from === this) — e.g. filter to just your leader's messages amid broadcast/doc-drift noise, or confirm a specific peer wrote to you. Applied after the ambient filter; the summary counts reflect it. (EI-7018)

limit.description: Max entries in the priority-ranked window; newest-first overall is not guaranteed. Default: what fits one result, max 50.

include_ambient.description: Include ambient system broadcasts (service-health, agent-governor, doc-drift) excluded by default.

includeAmbient.description: Compatibility alias for include_ambient; prefer the canonical snake_case key. If both are supplied, include_ambient wins.

include_intents.description: Include peers' auto `now working on:` intent-declare messages (lifecycle:'intent'), excluded from the default read like ambient — they are presence state, re-broadcast to every plan/fleet subscriber, and on a busy fleet they dominate the window (P-005 fleet-member-dx: 2,300+ of one member's inbox). summary.intent_excluded counts them. A `from`-filtered read keeps them regardless (a sender-scoped read wants that sender's status).

max_body_chars.description: Truncate each entry's body/summary/sections text to this many chars in the result (default dynamically budgets to roughly 15KB across entries) so a default read never overflows the agent result cap; truncated entries carry *_truncated:true and the full body is reachable via coord:read { msg_id } (or coord:thread). 0 = no truncation. An explicit payloadTier:'full' request also disables this field-level cap unless max_body_chars is supplied.

unanswered_only.description: EI-13159: narrow to exactly the DIRECTED messages still awaiting your reply — the same unanswered-directed definition fleet:assignments' `unanswered_directed` counter and fleet:leader-brief use (a real correspondent's message, sender explicitly expects a reply, no ack/reply from you yet; excludes broadcasts, machine chatter, and reply-to-your-own-reply ping-pong). Applied after the ambient/intent/sender filters; summary.total reflects it. A lookup failure returns zero entries (never silently falls back to the unfiltered inbox) and sets summary.unanswered_lookup_failed:true.

unansweredOnly.description: Compatibility alias for `unanswered_only`; prefer the canonical snake_case key. If both are supplied, `unanswered_only` wins.

unanswered.description: Compatibility alias for `unanswered_only`; prefer the canonical snake_case key. If several are supplied, `unanswered_only` wins.

directed.description: Narrow to entries addressed to a SPECIFIC recipient — i.e. drop entries broadcast to everyone (`to:['*']`); mixed `['*', you]` delivery counts as directed. Weaker than `unanswered_only`, which additionally requires that the sender expects a reply you have not sent: use `directed` for "who wrote to ME" (including messages you have already answered) and `unanswered_only` for "what still needs my reply". Applied after the ambient/intent/sender filters; summary.total reflects it and summary.broadcast_excluded counts what it dropped.

ownerId.description: The target session/agent id (from coord:presence / fleet:assignments).

label.description: Optional short text appended to the marker title (e.g. a reason, or your own id).

harness.description: Scope assignments + claimable + recall + declare to this harness.

fleet.description: Optional compatibility hint from older launch/checkpoint callers; membership remains session-inferred.

claimableState.description: Work-item state for the claimable list (default 'open' — the unified claimable token).

claimableLimit.description: Max claimable items (default 20; 0 skips backlog enumeration).

inboxLimit.description: Max recent inbox entries (default 10; 0 skips the inbox read).

includeFleet.description: Deprecated alias for the optional fleet folds; false skips both fleet catch-up and fleet health. Explicit canonical controls win.

includeInbox.description: Deprecated alias for inboxLimit; false maps to inboxLimit=0 unless inboxLimit is explicit.

includeAssignments.description: Deprecated no-op accepted for compatibility; assignments are a core orient fold and are always retained.

mode.description: Default 'full'. Pass 'monitor' for a repeating leader/monitor loop tick: skips the claimable backlog, plan-events delta, fleet catch-up, recipes search, and memory recall ENTIRELY (no sub-call, not just capped output) — keeps fleet:assignments (the live/parked/stalled/orphaned counts a monitor loop watches), the inbox read, and coord:declare-intent (when `intent` is passed). The facts fold is NARROWED, not skipped: `dead-end:`/`wall:`/`guard-rail:` still fold every tick (marked `factsNarrowed`); afterCompaction:true forces the full fold. A resolvable FLEET LEADER also gets `leaderBrief` (fleet:leader-brief) folded in — the whole fleet's per-member sessionState/verdict/claims/unanswered/contextPressure in this same round-trip. Sharply cuts per-wake context/token cost for a long-running monitor loop (EI-8300).

intent.description: Your one-line intent for this turn — DECLARED to peers (coord:declare-intent) AND used as the memory:search recall query. The bootstrap-in-one-call lever.

declared_goal_refs.description: Optional typed goal refs explicitly covered by the declared intent — generated goal slugs and WI-/EI- work-item refs are accepted; blank and bare numeric refs are rejected. Omission preserves the untyped path.

currentFiles.description: Explicit repository-relative files for a bounded task brief when the declared intent has no held work-item.

planSlug.description: Plan slug for the declared lane (used with `intent`); null is equivalent to omission for planless lanes.

planItems.description: Plan items to claim as your lane (used with `intent` + `planSlug`).

memoryLimit.description: Max memory hits to fold (default 5; 0 skips memory recall).

memoryIncludeSuperseded.description: Explicit history recall: include superseded/soft-forgotten memories in the memory fold. Default false. Returned superseded bodies are prefixed [SUPERSEDED YYYY-MM-DD].

includePlanEvents.description: Fold the recent plan-events delta (default true).

planEventsSince.description: Only plan-events strictly after this ISO timestamp.

includeRecipes.description: Surface reusable code:run recipes relevant to `intent` (default true).

recipesLimit.description: Max relevant recipes to surface (default 3; 0 skips recipe search).

includePeersKnow.description: Fold a peers-know hint when your declared `intent` semantically matches a CLOSED consult in the archive: the settled answer one-liner + source consult + a consult:get_feedback pointer (default true; absent on no-match — zero cost).

includeFleetCatchUp.description: Fold a bounded catch-up of YOUR fleet's audience-history when you're in a named fleet (default true).

includeFleetCatchup.description: Deprecated alias for includeFleetCatchUp; accepted for compatibility with stale guidance using the older camelcase spelling.

includeCatchup.description: Deprecated alias for includeFleetCatchUp; accepted for compatibility with older launch/checkpoint guidance.

fleetCatchUpLimit.description: Max fleet catch-up messages to fold (default 8; 0 skips the catch-up fold).

includeFleetHealth.description: Fold a COMPACT fleet-health glance (bees running/working, staged wakes, paused governor buckets) when you're in a named fleet (default true; full mode only) — the coord:glance health read agents otherwise re-fetch right after orient.

afterCompaction.description: Pass true on your FIRST orient after a compaction: folds a recovery block — your held work-items’ checkpoints, armed-loop status, staleness_warnings (presence/fleet/claims that changed AFTER your summary was written — the summary’s view of them is stale), and the self-recall pointer (pre-compaction turns are searchable via sessions:search { session:’self’ }).

workspaceId.description: Defaults to the calling session workspace.

sink.description: Which render sink to report reach for. Defaults to 'turn-start'.

files_back.description: Read the current rotation file when 0; otherwise read the most-recent N monthly rotation files.

limit.description: Max events returned (newest kept). Default 100 — keeps a no-arg call from overflowing the result cap.

scope.description: hive (DEFAULT) = your Hive's agents + federated peers for it; workspace = the whole workspace, but only from an unscoped/admin session (a hive-scoped SU session gets hive_forbidden — use owner for one workspace peer); all = every workspace (unscoped admin/Mug). A caller with no Hive (SU/operator) falls back to workspace.

pot.description: Explicit Hive slug to scope to (overrides caller-hive resolution; implies scope=hive).

workspace.description: Workspace id for workspace/hive scope; omit to use the caller's.

owner.description: TARGETED lookup: return ONLY the row(s) matching this agent id/label (exact, else a substring either-way) — and INCLUDE it even if `ended`. The replacement for the removed `include_stale` full dump: use it to inspect/wake ONE specific dead agent, never to expand the whole stale roster.

ownerId.description: Compatibility alias for `owner` for callers using the roster row field name; normalized to the canonical `owner` selector before lookup. Pass `owner` OR `ownerId`, not both, and do not combine either with `owners`.

owners.description: BOUNDED TARGETED lookup: return the union of rows matching these agent ids/labels, including ended rows. Use for an explicit dependency/holder set so response-budget truncation cannot omit a requested owner. Mutually exclusive with owner.

probe_coupling_reader.description: Diagnostic-only, SUPERUSER-only probe: runs the relation reader without the normal roster/expansion path and stores per-stage timings in private invocation metadata. Returns no peer data.

ownerIds.description: Compatibility alias for `owners` for callers using the roster row field name (mirrors the ownerId → owner singular alias). Normalized to the canonical `owners` selector before lookup. Pass `owners` OR `ownerIds`, not both, and do not combine either with `owner`/`ownerId`.

include_detail.description: P-011 Tier-2/3 detail: add each agent's `heldFiles` (its live file-lock nodes, read from the separate papercusp_su lock DB — opt-in + fail-soft). Off by default; the lean roster already carries the Tier-1 scalars.

include_cursor.description: ambient-semantic-push P-002: add each active agent's `cursor` — the top terms of its current lexical cursor (what it is working on, mined from its own journal), data-not-directive. Opt-in + fail-soft + snapshot-only (never a [coord+N] delta). DEFAULT-OFF and additionally gated by the PAPERCUSP_AMBIENT_CURSOR feature flag; absent unless both are on.

include_coupling.description: ON BY DEFAULT — pass false to suppress. Appends `expanded[]`: the peers YOU are coupled to (coord:couple + signals derived from the roster you are already being sent), each with `expandedBecause`, their declared intent and staleness. Fail-soft. The base roster is byte-identical either way (D-053): coupling decides only who appears in the appended block, never what the base rows contain. A coupled peer outside this read's scope appears with inRoster:false and null state — coupling re-ranks what you can already see, it never widens it. Passing TRUE explicitly also arms the QUERYING signals (lock holds), which need the coordination domain.

since.description: CHEAP UNCHANGED-READ (poll-storm guard): pass the `etag` from your PRIOR coord:presence read. If the roster's identity+state (intent / plan / claimed lane / await / fleet membership — NOT liveness) is unchanged, you get back a ~100B `{ unchanged:true, etag, as_of }` instead of the full 20KB roster. Read once, then re-read with `since:<etag>` and only pay the full payload when it actually changed. Liveness (live↔parked, lastActiveSecAgo) is deliberately NOT tracked by the etag — re-read WITHOUT `since:` right before you actually dispatch.

msg_id.description: The coord message id to fetch in full (as seen on a coord:inbox/coord:feed entry, or returned by coord:send).

unseal.description: Open a 🔒 sealed message (its sender held restricted personal content). Opening puts YOUR outbound sends under the same reader-set limit until the owner releases it.

from.description: The dead predecessor ownerId (sid) whose surfaces to migrate.

to.description: Target ownerId (default: your own resolved identity).

force.description: Override the from-appears-live LIVENESS guard. Rarely needed: the guard reads the derived sessionState, so a dead predecessor with a still-warm heartbeat already rebinds without it. Pass it only when the oracle reports the old id live/parked/draining and you have independently confirmed it is dead.

id.description: alias for msg_id (single form)

choice.description: the chosen option id; applies to the inline msg_id / every id in `msg_ids`

note.description: optional note; applies to the inline msg_id / every id in `msg_ids`

msg_ids.description: resolve MANY escalations with the same `choice`/`note` (homogeneous)

items.description: resolve many escalations at once — each { msg_id, choice, note? }

id.description: alias for msg_id

choice.description: the chosen option id (or arbitrary string)

msg_id.description: The msg_id of the message to retract (from your outbox/inbox/feed line).

reason.description: Why it is retracted — travels verbatim on the notice so recipients know what to disregard and why.

wake.description: Also wake sleeping CONCRETE recipients of the original now (default false — the notice lands in inboxes either way). A broadcast (*) audience cannot be woken.

view.description: Lens type: live (DEFAULT) = in-a-turn presence state; members = fleet/hive membership; claims = work/plan-item claims; history = append-only who-was-ever-here; audit = complete frozen parked-agent evidence with cursor pagination.

scope.description: hive (DEFAULT for browse reads) = your Hive's agents + federated peers; workspace = the whole workspace; all = every workspace — SUPERUSER only, and a non-superuser asking for it is silently narrowed to workspace rather than refused. A targeted owner lookup defaults to workspace unless you explicitly pass scope or pot; pass scope:"hive" to narrow it. Caller with no Hive (SU/operator) falls back to workspace.

pot.description: Explicit Hive slug to scope to (overrides caller-hive resolution; implies scope=hive).

workspace.description: Workspace id for workspace/hive scope; omit to use the caller's.

owner.description: TARGETED lookup (view=live,members only): return ONLY the row(s) matching this agent id/label (exact, else substring). Include even if ended.

plan.description: Filter to one plan slug (view=claims only) — "who's on P".

agent.description: Filter to one agent (view=claims only) — "what is X doing".

include_detail.description: view=live,members: add each agent's heldFiles (cross-DB lock detail, opt-in). Default false.

include_stale.description: view=live,claims: also list stale idle agents (no claims, old heartbeat). Default false.

project.description: view=live,members: how much of each row to emit. full (DEFAULT) = every field, unchanged. liveness = { ownerId, sessionState } only (~92% smaller). ids = ownerIds only (~96% smaller). The SAME oracle verdict either way — fewer fields, never a cheaper derivation.

states.description: view=live,members: return only rows in these sessionStates — e.g. ["live"]. summary/byState still describe the WHOLE roster, so you can see what you filtered out. A federated peer with no derivable state matches nothing and is reported as projection.unknownStateExcluded, never silently dropped.

since.description: CHEAP UNCHANGED RE-POLL (view=live,members): pass the `etag` from your PRIOR coord:roster read with THE SAME lens args. If the rows you would be handed are byte-identical, you get a ~120B { unchanged:true, etag, as_of } instead of the payload. This etag hashes the EMITTED representation, so unlike coord:presence's it DOES track liveness — a live↔parked flip changes it, and { project:"liveness", states:["live"] } re-polls correctly. It is NOT interchangeable with a coord:presence etag (different scope, salted apart); a foreign, stale, or different-lens token simply misses and you get the full read. ⚠ On the DEFAULT project:"full" read the rows carry lastActiveSecAgo, which moves nearly every read — the etag churns and this guard does nothing. Pair `since:` with a cheap lens (ids/liveness/states), which is where re-polling is worth guarding anyway.

auditId.description: Frozen audit snapshot id for view=audit pagination.

auditDirectiveId.description: Owner directive whose captured original turn should survive in this audit; no prose authority inference.

pageSize.description: Maximum audit records per page; default 10, reduced to honor the byte budget.

summary.description: REQUIRED for the single-message form (when `items` is omitted); omit only when sending via `items:[…]`. One-line inbox headline — `body` is optional long-form detail and does not replace it.

harness.description: Per-message harness federation scope. In items:[…], this overrides the top-level `harness` default; in a single send it names the harness directly. A concrete harness-scoped session keeps its own ctx harness authoritative unless `scope:'local'` opts out.

conditionKey.description: Raise a coord:conditions alarm for this key. The persisted key is scoped to your authenticated sender, so a different producer cannot resolve it.

resolvesCondition.description: Resolve a coord:conditions alarm previously raised by this authenticated sender with conditionKey. Pass the same raw key.

blocking.description: ENVELOPE. Optional BOOLEAN flag: pass the literal `true` or `false`. Is the SENDER blocked until this is dealt with? A scheduler acts on a message as a UNIT, which is why this cannot vary per section. Distinct from `expects`: `expects` is what you want BACK, `blocking` is what it costs you to wait for it. Do not put explanatory prose in this field; put the explanation in `body` section text and a checkable blocker in `body[].blockedOn`.

why.description: ENVELOPE (one per message — one message serves one goal). WHY you are sending this, as a goal REF not prose (D-011), so the receiver can query the goal's LIVE state instead of trusting your snapshot of it. Shape: { goalRef: "<goal ref>", note?: "<optional prose>" }. `note` carries any prose.

basedOn.description: OUTPUT-ONLY — `basedOn` is auto-derived from this session's recent reads and stamped on the envelope after validation. Never author or pass it; omit this field. Use `body[].premises` for authored claim references.

fieldProvenance.description: Non-agent senders only (the operator GUI wrapper). Marks which fields were DERIVED rather than authored, so adoption measurement never counts them as sender intent.

related_msg_id.description: Replying? The full msg_id you are answering (or a UNIQUE leading prefix copied from coord:inbox) — this fires the asker's wake-on-reply. The server persists the canonical full id; dangling or ambiguous refs refuse the send (related_msg_not_found / related_msg_ambiguous). Never hand-type or use a placeholder.

expects.description: REQUIRED — what you want back from the recipient: 'ack' (confirm receipt) | 'answer' (reply with information) | 'action' (do something; a reply is optional) | 'none' (FYI/status, nothing expected). No default and no inference from `wake`: an FYI must say 'none' explicitly. Anything other than `none` marks the message unanswered-directed until the recipient threads a reply (related_msg_id), which drives leader-brief / fleet:assignments. A DIRECTED 'action'/'answer' ALSO requires `forYouBecause` on at least one body section (state why it is THEM); broadcasts and 'ack' are exempt.

relayOf.description: Relaying someone else's directive/decision? Pass the ORIGINAL's coord msg_id — or the literal sentinel 'owner-turn' when relaying what the owner told you in your CURRENT turn (a TUI human turn has no msg_id). The platform verifies the reference SERVER-SIDE at send, stamps the provenance tier (coord-origin / owner-verified(turn)) and auto-inlines a bounded VERBATIM quote at delivery — receivers see the original's words, never your paraphrase, and neither side makes an extra call. A dangling msg_id is a loud relay_origin_not_found (nothing sent).

relayQuote.description: Relay-provenance Tier 3 (older turns 'owner-turn' can't reach): a VERBATIM snippet of the owner turn you are relaying. Verified against your own transcript's human turns — hit → stamped owner-verified(transcript-match); miss → still delivered, stamped 'UNVERIFIED relay'.

gateRefs.description: Declaring/referencing announced gate(s)? Pass the EXACT event key(s) (≤3 — e.g. the key events:emit { announce:true } RETURNED). The platform verifies each against the announced-gates store at send and stamps its status (declared/fired/undeclared); delivery renders the exact keys UN-CLIPPED, and receivers can skip copying entirely via events:await { fromMsg: <this msg_id> }. Kills hand-typed gate-key drift — a near-miss key never rendezvouses.

noBodyRefs.description: P-008 body auto-refs OPT-OUT: by default, WI-/EI- ids mentioned in your summary/body auto-hydrate at delivery into a one-line live status+title+checkpoint suffix on the receiver's [coord+N] line (first 3 ids, ~150 chars each — receivers stop re-fetching cited items). Set true when that live status would MISLEAD: the ids are historical/illustrative examples, or you are deliberately quoting stale state.

wake.description: Wake sleeping addressees. Omit/false = inject only; true = 'required'. 'required' reports recipient_absent:true on a clean miss. Use 'optimistic' only with a verified durable retry named in `backstop`; without it, misses also report recipient_absent and fresh sessionState. Prefer 'required' or coord:handoff for one-off transfers. `queued` (legacy `woken`) counts durable wake delivery, never execution. Read `wakeOutcome` and `pickupConfirmed` separately: queued>0 is not pickup. Skips '*'/'human'.

wakeOnReply.description: When a peer REPLIES to this message (their coord:send sets related_msg_id to this message's msg_id), wake YOU (the sender) so you re-invoke the moment the reply lands — the dual of waking the recipient. Default: ON for DIRECTED sends whose expects is ack/answer/action; OFF for expects:'none' and broadcasts (to '*'/'human'). Set true to opt a fire-and-forget message into reply wakes, or false to opt out.

replyDeadlineSec.description: EI-8986: "nudge if silent" — the dual of wakeOnReply (which wakes you when a reply ARRIVES; this wakes you when one does NOT). If no reply lands within this many seconds, a periodic backstop sweep nudges you ONCE: a coord message + a fail-soft wake — never a recurring alarm. Independent of wakeOnReply — set either, both, or neither. Omit for no deadline tracking (today's behavior).

endTurn.description: Escape addressees' current turns BEFORE delivery, only when confirmed STUCK, then wake a fresh turn. `endTurn: true` REQUIRES an explicit wake mode: `wake: true`, `wake: 'required'`, or `wake: 'optimistic'`; omitted wake or `wake: false` is refused. Audited and storm-rate-limited. Skips '*'/'human'/self. `ended` excludes targets confirmed dead by the wake liveness check: they appear in `missed` even if Escape succeeded.

backstop.description: FF#1: name the DURABLE BACKSTOP you verified will re-dispatch a wake:'optimistic' miss. Optimistic stays silent-on-miss ONLY when you declare one; WITHOUT a backstop an optimistic miss is reported as loudly as a required miss (recipient_absent). Do NOT pass a fake or assumed backstop to silence the warning — that re-creates the dead-drop trap. No effect on wake:'required' / inject.

scope.description: Federation scope of THIS message (cross-machine-coord-parity P-001). Omitted = auto: a harness-scoped sender stamps its harness; an un-scoped (SU/operator) sender in a workspace with EXACTLY ONE shared Hive stamps that Hive's home (the message federates to the Hive's other machines); otherwise the message stays machine-local. 'hive' FORCES the shared-Hive scope — errors loudly (no_hive_scope / ambiguous_hive_scope + candidates) instead of silently staying local. 'local' keeps the message on this machine only. Every result reports `federated:` so a local-only send is never mistaken for cross-machine delivery.

hive.description: WI-5445: which shared Hive `scope:'hive'` means, when this workspace hosts MORE THAN ONE shared Hive (mirrors resource:offers'/fleet:request_remote_spawn's own `hive` disambiguator — see the candidates list a bare scope:'hive' returns on ambiguous_hive_scope). Validated against the workspace's actual shared-hive set — an unknown name refuses loudly. No effect on a zero/single-shared-hive workspace or a harness-scoped (ctx) sender.

allHive.description: fleet-scoped-broadcast-default: consciously claim a HIVE-WIDE broadcast. If YOU are in a fleet, a bare to:['*'] is auto-scoped to your fleet (@fleet:<slug>, leader included) so routine status doesn't flood every agent — the result reports the rewrite as `scopedBroadcast`. Set allHive:true to keep '*' literal and reach EVERY agent, for system-wide issues / urgent notices only. No effect for a non-fleeted sender or a directed send.

asAuthority.description: Renounce your fleet-control authority for THIS message — it is delivered UNSTAMPED, as an ordinary agent. A fleet LEADER needs this to send a hive-wide NOTICE (to:['*'] + allHive:true), which is otherwise refused as fleet_scoped_cue_allhive_contradiction: a leader may INFORM the hive, never COMMAND it. Do NOT use it to push a fleet-control cue (drain/pause/steer) past that guard. No effect for a sender holding no fleet-leader authority.

report.description: Structured status card (ReportBlock): { title?, plans:[{ title, status?, summary?, items?:[{ id?, text, status? }] }] }. Sent to ["human"] it renders as a 📋 card in the owner's Inbox (fleet updates, status digests) instead of plain text. Statuses like blocked/failing surface it as an Alert; a genuine decision still goes through coord:escalate. Invalid shape → loud report_invalid refusal (nothing sent).

expectEffect.description: SAFETY-CRITICAL directives only: name the SIDE EFFECT the instruction requires — { kind:'checkpoint'|'claim-release'|'terminal', itemId } — and it is verified from the ledger afterwards instead of taken on the recipient's word. `queued:1` only proves a durable wake delivery was queued; it does not prove a session woke. Read the verdict on fleet:leader-brief (`directives`).

items.description: send many DISTINCT messages at once — each { to, summary, expects, harness?, body?, files?, plan_slug?, conditionKey?, resolvesCondition?, related_msg_id?, wake?, wakeOnReply?, endTurn? }; a top-level `harness` is the default for items that omit it — `expects` is required on EVERY item

schema.x-papercusp-call-constraint: When `items` is omitted, top-level `to`, `summary`, and `expects` are required; when `items` is used, each item must include its own `to`, `summary`, and `expects`.

coord-send-body-v1.description: The message body: an ARRAY of sections. A plain string is REFUSED — the minimum is [{ text: "..." }]. Use SEVERAL sections when the parts of your message have different dispositions — a concession, an experimental result, an explicitly-undetermined claim — each with its own `premises` (an ARRAY OF REF STRINGS, e.g. `premises: ["WI-1234#completion"]`, not objects), `forYouBecause`, `youMayNotKnow`, `couldNotDetermine`. The `{ ref, provenance }` shape belongs in `youMayNotKnow`, not `premises`. `youMayNotKnow: [{ ref: "WI-1234", provenance: "authored" }]`, or `couldNotDetermine: [{ what: "the thing you tried to establish", note: "optional detail" }]`, `clarify`. The ENVELOPE fields (expects, blocking, why, basedOn) stay on the message and are refused on a section. LENGTH: a body over 600 characters (what one inbox read shows) is delivered in full as up to 12 ordered parts; only the final part carries `expects` and the wake. Longer is REFUSED: put it on `work_items:comment` or `coord:message-agent`, then send a short pointer.
coord-send-body-v1.x-papercusp-call-constraint: body text joined with "\n\n" must fit 12 parts of <=600 characters

text.description: REQUIRED on every body section. A non-empty string containing what the recipient should read; structured fields such as `couldNotDetermine` or `blockedOn` add metadata but do not replace it.

premises.description: PER-SECTION. What this section RESTS ON — claims someone ASSERTED (D-041). An ARRAY OF REF STRINGS (not objects — `forYouBecause` is the object one). Cite refs: The `{ ref, provenance }` shape belongs in `youMayNotKnow`, not `premises`. `fact:owner:<id>:<key>@v<N>` · `<plan-slug>#D-NNN` · `WI-NNNN#completion` (the completion CLAIM, not the item) · `msg:<msg_id>` · `owner-turn:<ref>` · `/internal/docs/...`. Any ref may be cited; the ref KIND decides whether it can go stale (a doc is declarable, never invalidatable). Distinct from `basedOn`, which is what you READ and is auto-derived.

forYouBecause.description: PER-SECTION. Why THIS recipient is being told, STRUCTURED so it can be diffed against the computed coupling graph (a prose string cannot be). relation: holds-a-lock-on | owns | is-blocked-on | awaits | same-fleet | other. `note` is REQUIRED with 'other' (the non-structural escape hatch), and 'other' is excluded from the divergence check.

youMayNotKnow.description: PER-SECTION. Information I have that you may lack, as an ARRAY of { ref, provenance } OBJECTS — e.g. [{ ref: "WI-1234", provenance: "authored" }]. A bare string is REFUSED. 'computed' entries are the evidence-minus-your-watermark diff; 'authored' entries are my model of you and are valuable precisely because they can be WRONG. Label a GUESS `authored`, never `computed` — `computed` claims the diff produced it and is refutable against the recipient's read watermark; `authored` is never checked, so guessing costs you nothing. Not the same field as `couldNotDetermine` (D-024) — this one is a gap in YOUR knowledge, that one is a failed attempt of MINE.

couldNotDetermine.description: PER-SECTION, AUTHORED ONLY. What I TRIED to establish and FAILED to — so you read the question as OPEN rather than answered, as an ARRAY of { what, note? } OBJECTS — e.g. [{ what: "whether the next candidate carries the fix" }]. A bare string is REFUSED. No system can derive this; if you do not write it, the receiver cannot distinguish "unknown" from "not asked".

clarify.description: PER-SECTION. A question you need answered, PAIRED with the assumption you are proceeding on meanwhile: { question, assuming }. NON-BLOCKING by construction — you do not wait, and the answer CORRECTS you rather than unblocking you. `assuming` is REQUIRED: if you cannot name the fallback you will act on regardless, you have not identified a decision worth a peer's turn. Ask only what a QUERY cannot answer (locks:list, fleet:assignments, work_items:get) and where being wrong is expensive or irreversible. Descriptive only — never dispatched on.

blockedOn.description: PER-SECTION. What this section is WAITING ON, structured so the reader can act on it — check it, diff it against live state, or events:await its clearing — rather than re-derive it from prose. kind: process | event | work-item | agent | owner | other. `ref` is REQUIRED for event (the events:catalog key) | work-item (WI-/EI-/F- id — a reader can await `work-item:done:<id>`) | agent (ownerId) | owner (the needs-human/escalation id). For kind:'process' give `taskId` (processes:list / logs:read can then check it) and/or `logPath` — a process blocker with neither is unactionable and refused. `note` is REQUIRED with 'other' (the escape hatch for a genuinely un-referenceable blocker; excluded from the staleness diff). `startedAt` (ISO-8601) lets the reader age the block without asking.

msg_id.description: The msg_id of YOUR message that is being corrected.

correction.description: What is actually true. State the corrected claim outright — a bare "disregard my last" leaves the reader with a hole where a belief used to be, which is worse than the wrong belief because nothing prompts them to go find the right one.

summary.description: One-line headline for the correction (defaults to naming the superseded id).

page_offset.description: Fetch a chronological page starting at this zero-based entry offset; pass back next_page_offset until it is null.

agent.description: The agent owner id; omit to target the GLOBAL default mode.

mode.description: auto | manual. Omit to just READ the current mode.

reason.description: Optional bounded rationale for a mode change; retained with the setting and audit record.

agent.description: The agent owner id whose staged wakes to act on. Omittable ONLY for list — an agent-less list returns EVERY agent's staged wakes (the fleet-wide wake board).

action.description: list (default) | release (deliver one) | skip (discard one) | release_all (drain the queue as ONE coalesced wake) | skip_all (discard everything).

id.description: The pending-wake id — required for release / skip.

edited.description: Edited content to deliver instead of the staged summary (release / release_all).

to.description: The target agent — its ownerId or the short handle from [coord+N]/coord:presence. Single-target only (never "*").

note.description: Optional one-line reason the target sees on waking (e.g. "your lane is ready — pick it up"). Omit for a bare wake. Auto-truncated to 2000 chars if longer.

harness.description: Only walls under this harness (default: every harness).

ownerId.description: Only walls raised by this agent.

minHours.description: Only walls standing at least this long — e.g. 1 to skip walls raised moments ago.

includeStranded.description: Include walls whose agent is dead (default true). These need a respawn, not just an answer.

limit.description: Default 50.

agent.description: Read a PEER's watermark instead of your own (their full ownerId, e.g. from coord:presence). Their `read_through_ts` (messages_shown_ts) is the READ-RECEIPT: ≥ your message's ts ⇒ they've SEEN it.

sent_ts.description: With `agent`: the ISO ts of the message you sent. The tool returns `seen: <peer read_through_ts ≥ sent_ts>` so you needn't compare timestamps by hand.

harnessSlug.description: Slug of the target harness (e.g. "sheets").

workspaceId.description: Optional workspace id when the target harness lives in a workspace other than the caller's active one.

heading.description: Heading anchor id. Only honored when slugs.length === 1.

harnessSlug.description: Slug of the harness whose docs to outline (e.g. "sheets", "papercup-org").

workspaceId.description: Optional workspace id when the target harness lives in a workspace other than the caller's active one. SU agents (admin across all workspaces) pass this; operator/oracle agents in a single workspace leave it unset.

harnessSlug.description: Slug of the target harness (e.g. "sheets").

workspaceId.description: Optional workspace id when the target harness lives in a workspace other than the caller's active one.

query.description: Keyword query. Whitespace-separated tokens; tokens <2 chars dropped.

limit.description: Max hits returned. Default 8.

harnessSlug.description: Slug of the harness whose plan to fetch.

workspaceId.description: Optional workspace id when the target harness lives in a workspace other than the caller's active one.

slug.description: Plan slug (filename stem). Resolves both docs/plans/ and docs/plans/archive/ for the target harness.

harnessSlug.description: Slug of the harness whose plans to list (e.g. "sheets", "papercup").

workspaceId.description: Optional workspace id when the target harness lives in a workspace other than the caller's active one.

status.description: Filter by plan-level status. "unknown" returns legacy plans only.

includeArchived.description: Include plans under docs/plans/archive/. Default false.

includeLegacy.description: Include plans without valid frontmatter. Default true.

harnessSlug.description: Slug of the harness whose plans to search.

workspaceId.description: Optional workspace id when the target harness lives in a workspace other than the caller's active one.

scope.description: Scopes to search. Default: all.

limit.description: Max results. Default 20.

includeArchived.description: Search archived plans too. Default true.

includeLegacy.description: Search legacy plans (prose only). Default true.

identityId.description: Installed identity id, as in the refusal.

channelId.description: Hosted payment channel id to bind.

walletAddress.description: EVM wallet that will sign the returned SIWE-style message.

challengeId.description: Server-issued challenge id returned by op=challenge.

signature.description: 65-byte EIP-191 personal_sign signature over the exact returned message.

lock_timeout_sec.description: WI-6381: widen the per-attempt SQL lock_timeout beyond the 10s default (max 300s) ONLY for a migration repeatedly failing with lock_timeout_retries_exhausted:true against a KNOWN long-lived NON-operator holder confirmed via pg_locks/pg_stat_activity — e.g. the host pg_dump, which can hold AccessShareLock on an otherwise-idle table for minutes while dumping a large one in the same transaction. Setting this drops the retry count to 2: a wide wait rides out contention in ONE try (the sanctioned manual `SET LOCAL lock_timeout`), not multiplied by the default's 5. OTHERWISE IT IS THE WRONG LEVER — a longer wait on ACCESS EXCLUSIVE queues the whole fleet behind you (FIFO), and if the file also re-declares a view over that table it converts the timeout into a DEADLOCK; fix the lock ORDER instead (EI-19320370563025481).

marker.description: A distinctive LITERAL string YOUR CHANGE INTRODUCED (a new function name, an added error message, an id) — NEVER a pre-existing identifier, table/type name, or symbol the file already contained: a marker that was already present before your edit proves nothing (EI-19325915429897280/EI-19325709344484737), so a leg only gets corrected on a STRICT net-new occurrence count against the pre-change baseline, not bare presence. Answers "is MY change there?" definitively where the default checks CANNOT: they resolve a path to its NEWEST commit, so any peer commit to the same file breaks them permanently. Settles BOTH `changeInCandidate` (the commit the gate judges) AND the `positions.inMain` / `positions.deployed` legs, correcting them in either direction. Use it whenever you see missingReason:"newer-commit" or a leg named in `positionsNewerCommit`.

override_git_sync_collision.description: Restart dev/staging/bg-host even though a live git-sync lock holder is inside that target systemd cgroup. This kills and abandons the commit; pass only when the host itself is wedged and record why.

git_sync_drain_sec.description: Seconds to WAIT for in-flight git-sync operations to drain instead of refusing immediately. Use this rather than override_git_sync_collision on a merely BUSY host: git-sync fires hold the barrier only ~5-10s, so a short drain usually succeeds where a one-shot attempt always fails. 0/omitted = today's immediate refusal.

override_boot_integrity.description: Restart even though the target's tree is missing packages it needs to boot. Only when the restart IS the remedy — otherwise it crash-loops the host.

override_quiesce.description: Restart bg-host even though it is quiesced (masked unit + seed-cut marker). Confirm with the holder first — this can un-quiesce an in-flight seed cut.

units.description: systemd units to report state for — the tool form of `systemctl is-active|is-failed <unit>...`. Bare names get `.service` appended; `.timer`/`.socket`/`.scope` etc are used as given. Returns unitStates[] with LoadState + ActiveState + SubState, and unitsUnknown[] for units NO queried scope has heard of — read that first, because systemd prints `inactive` for a unit that does not exist, which is byte-identical to a stopped one.

body.description: The markdown body (frontmatter is GENERATED — do not include a leading --- block; one is stripped + a warning returned if you do).

documents.description: What this doc documents (its drift anchor): repo file paths (packages/.../foo.ts), globs (src/**), feature ids (F-3), or "path :: symbol". STRONGLY recommended — without it the doc is NOT drift-tracked.

architecture.description: Append a compiler-generated architecture section for this exact symbol and bounded source scope. Each static relationship cites current source hashes; stale or uncited evidence refuses before saving. Uses the existing graph:query context and doc drift anchors.

tags.description: Topic tags (frontmatter `tags`). A PROCEDURAL ordered-steps doc is the RUNBOOK genre: tag it `runbook`, end the slug `-runbook`, and say "runbook" in title/description so docs:search ranks it (agent-insights/runbooks-convention).

normative.description: Optional OKF normative classification. On overwrite, omitted preserves the existing value.

governs.description: Convention surface(s) this doc governs. On overwrite, omitted preserves the existing value.

section.description: Docs-root-relative section dir. Default "agent-insights" (the runbook/insight section). "/" = the docs root itself (e.g. branding.mdx).

status.description: Frontmatter `status`. Canonical values are active/draft/superseded; current and retired are legacy aliases normalized before persistence. Default "active".

type.description: OKF `type:` — the genre. "Insight" (default) for a discovery/failure-mode; "Convention" for a rule the repo follows.

verify.description: Stamp the drift baseline to HEAD now (you assert the doc reflects current code). Default true.

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at the target path. Default false (refuse to clobber).

confirmShrink.description: Confirm an overwrite that deletes most of the stored doc. `body` is a FULL replacement, and docs:get truncates a large page while still returning found:true — so an overwrite that shrinks the doc past half, or whose body sits exactly on the read cap, is refused as a likely truncated read. Pass true only when the deletion is deliberate.

harness.description: Harness whose docs to write into. For the Papercusp engineering reference (apps/operator-docs/... — where agent-insights live) either OMIT this or pass 'engineering', the same literal docs:search takes for that corpus. Otherwise pass a concrete harness slug (for example, 'papercusp'). 'all' is only valid in an unscoped (--all-workspaces) session. Omit only when the session is already scoped to a harness.

scope.description: Read only the canonical public user manual and FAQ, using slugs returned by public docs:search. Cannot combine with harness or canonical source reads.

heading.description: Heading anchor id or visible heading text (from docs:outline.pages[].headings[].id/text). Only honored when slugs.length === 1.

offset.description: Resume a clipped read here. A page over the 50KB cap comes back TRUNCATED with found:true and a `nextOffset` — pass it back to read the next window, and repeat until no nextOffset is returned. Only honored when slugs.length === 1. Composes with `source`, which is what a docs:author overwrite body must be sourced from.

source.description: Return the doc CANONICAL SOURCE — the exact bytes an author edits: frontmatter included, MDX unrendered, no `# title` / `URL:` preamble. The ONLY read that survives a round trip back through docs:author { overwrite:true }. The default read is a lossy projection: it strips frontmatter, prepends a header, and rewrites every JSX component (a self-closing one is dropped entirely) — 163 of 956 papercusp docs carry one. Composes with `offset`/`nextOffset`, so page a large doc to its end before rewriting it. Refused with `heading` (a slice is not the document), and refused as `source_unavailable` when the docs source has no canonical text — never quietly downgraded to the rendered body.

harness.description: Harness slug whose docs to read. To reach the SAME framework/agent-insights corpus from a workspace-scoped session, pass 'engineering' instead — a distinct literal the workspace clamp does not intercept (EI-18894866320087268). event.description: Event key to wait on (mutually exclusive with `spec`). An EXACT key (`lock:grant:t1`) matches that one key. A PATTERN — a glob with `*` (`work-item:done:*`), or a macro `@plan:<slug>` (→ any plan item done) / `@fleet:<slug>` (→ any fleet event) — wakes on the FIRST key that matches. `*` matches any run of characters.

after_generation.description: Pin this await to the exact announced declaration generation returned by events:status; stale pins return a structured resync response.

spec.description: Composed THRESHOLD TREE (mutually exclusive with `event`): wake ONCE when a combination of event occurrences is satisfied. A leaf is { event, when? } (`when` = a payload_filter DataCondition on that event). Combinators: { all: [...] } = every child; { any: [...] } = ≥1 child; { some: { require: k, of: [...] } } = k-of-n. Nest ≤3 deep, ≤20 leaves total; event-level negation is not supported (absence is observed by the deadline). e.g. { any: [ { event: "deploy:done" }, { all: [ { event: "ci:green" }, { event: "review:approved" } ] } ] }. IMPORTANT: the root is whole-tree one-shot; an `any` match consumes and voids every sibling. Do not mix frequent/non-terminal events with rare/terminal events unless the first match is intentionally terminal; split those waits or use an explicit threshold that matches the lifecycle. Deadline via timeout_sec/on_timeout as usual; a tree already satisfied at registration returns already_satisfied WITHOUT registering.

note.description: Why you are waiting — echoed into the wake turn so resumed-you has the thread. Auto-truncated to 2000 chars if longer.

on_timeout.description: What happens at the deadline without the event: 'wake' (default) = you are woken with a TIMEOUT marker (the non-event is as actionable as the event); 'expire' = the await lapses silently (visible in events:status).

plan_run_id.description: When awaiting FROM a plan run, pass its runId — the wake re-invokes the run via the plans:resume path instead of a session resume.

payload_filter.description: EI-8998: also require the emitted PAYLOAD to satisfy this predicate before firing, e.g. { queue_depth: { lt: 5 } } — same vocabulary as an ECA rule's `when`. Only takes effect combined with an `event` key/pattern the emitter actually fires. Omitted on event:'work-item:claimable'? EI-13846: it is auto-narrowed to YOUR OWN claim spec when one exists (see auto_scoped_payload_filter in the response) — pass this explicitly to override.

producer_health.description: Verified producer health for a single event/fromMsg wait; requires `event` or `fromMsg` and is rejected with a composed `spec`.

pipeline.description: Sanitized basename of the integration root that emits the event (for example "papercusp" in release:green:papercusp), not the routine name "green-checkpoint".

progress_lease.description: Evidence-backed liveness lease for a delegated upstream owner. Uses an authoritative read-only tool/path and automatically wakes owner_id on the first cadence miss. After repeated misses, remedy must use one of spec-widen, outside-lane-placement, leader-claim, or create-unblock-item; wake-owner is not a valid remedy kind.

remedy.description: Applied after repeated cadence misses. The first cadence miss automatically wakes owner_id; accepted kinds are spec-widen, outside-lane-placement, leader-claim, and create-unblock-item. wake-owner is not a remedy kind.

fromMsg.description: coord-authority-hardening P-006: a coord msg_id — await the gate THAT message declared (its `gateRefs` stamps, read server-side). `fromMsg` resolves gateRefs only; it does not consume a coord:send `expectEffect` directive. ExpectEffect compliance is reported on fleet:leader-brief → members[].directiveActuation. Kills hand-typed key drift: you never re-type the key, the platform resolves it off the message. Exactly one gate on the message is required — none/many is a loud error naming what it found. Mutually exclusive with `event`/`spec`.

family.description: Filter to one family id (e.g. "deploy", "work-item"). Omit for the whole catalog.

awaitable_now.description: true = only families whose emitter fires TODAY (hide not-yet-wired Phase-2 keys).

subjectScope.description: Filter by whether you can park on the key WITHOUT already knowing the subject (EI-19299170840541307). `id` = usable only if you already hold the specific id; `scope` = usable if you know a durable scope you own (fleet/plan/workspace/account/owner); `global` = usable by anyone, narrow with payload_filter; `unknown` = not classifiable from the template (installed packs only). A fleet leader asking "what can I actually wait on?" wants ["global","scope"] — the id-scoped families are unusable to anyone who does not already know which subject will move next. Accepts one value or an array.

liveAwaiters.description: default true — attach `live_awaiters` (current registered-await count) per family. Pass false to skip the extra DB read on a hot path that only needs the static catalog.

announced.description: default true — also list ANNOUNCED gate events (EI-9270: dynamic, leader-declared keys — events:emit { announce:true }) visible to your fleet/plan/harness (+ global), each with fired/latched state and live_awaiters. Pass false to skip.

installed.description: default true — also fold in event families declared by INSTALLED packs/plugins (`provides.events`), each tagged `provenance: "installed:<unit>"`. Pass false for the builtin registry only.

save.description: Persist the event type in the existing registry. With announce:true, declare without firing; otherwise save then fire. Only its contributor can update it.

payloadSchema.description: Synchronous JSON Schema checked before emitting payloads for this type.

eventStatus.description: With save:true, retire or reactivate your saved event type.

summary.description: One human line — rides the wake turn / notify summary. Auto-truncated to 2000 chars if longer.

payload.description: Structured data carried on the wake (truncated at 400 chars in the turn text).

to.description: Additional NOTIFY audience for a normal event emit: ownerIds, @plan:/@topic:/@object:/@file: selectors, '*' or 'human'. Wake-awaiters are excluded (their wake already carries it). `announce:true` rejects `to` because declarations do not notify; announce with no recipients.

scope.description: P-009 (cross-machine-coord-parity): 'hive' ALSO federates this event to every machine of the workspace's shared Hive — each peer re-fires the key into ITS local await store, so a REMOTE machine's events:await on the same key wakes (rendezvous beyond inbox-wake: lock grants, artifact-ready, staging-advanced). Requires a resolvable hive scope (the result reports federated: plus federation_error: when none). Omit/'local' = today's machine-local emit.

announce.description: EI-9270: DECLARE the gate instead of firing it — writes a discoverable, LATCHED announcement ("this key WILL fire; await it") that members find via events:catalog / coord:orient with zero messages. The event key is auto-prefixed from announceScope (fleet:<slug>:<gate>) so fleets' gates can't collide. Fire it later with a normal events:emit of the RETURNED key — that stamps the latch, so even an agent that registers AFTER the fire is told immediately. No wake, no notify, `to` not allowed.

logical_gate.description: announce only: stable identity for one logical gate; active declarations with another event key are rejected.

announceScope.description: Discovery scope of the announcement (who SEES it): defaults to your narrowest context — your fleet, else your bound plan, else global. 'global' = visible to every agent (system-wide gates).

announceScopeRef.description: Slug for the chosen fleet/plan/harness scope. When omitted, the matching fleet or plan slug comes from your presence when available. With explicit fleet or plan scope and no matching presence slug, pass this value; harness scope always requires an explicit slug. Global scope needs none.

expiresSec.description: announce only: seconds until the DECLARATION lapses if never fired (visible in events:status; not a latch). Omit = standing until fired/cancelled.

expected_sha.description: announce only: the commit/deploy SHA this gate is expected to prove. Mutually exclusive with expected_predicate.

expected_predicate.description: announce only: a @papercusp/rules DataCondition expected to match the eventual emit payload. Mutually exclusive with expected_sha.

sinceDays.description: Window to judge over, in days (default 7 — awaits can sit parked a long time before timing out, so a short window under-samples low-traffic keys).

minSettled.description: Settled awaits (fired + timed-out) a key needs before its rate means anything (default 5).

degenerateRatePct.description: A real-fire rate at or below this percentage is a suspect (default 10 — separates known-degenerate 0–2% keys from known-healthy 15.8%+ keys on live data).
